w: This Scaliger-era fortress guards the entrance to Sirmione's old town on Lake Garda and ranks among Italy's best-preserved castles. Ringed by its own moat fed by the lake, it drew 262,095 visitors in 2024 alone, making it the 29th most-visited attraction in the country that year.
s: Moated castle guarding Sirmione's lakefront old town
_facts: 262,095 visitors in 2024; 29th most-visited site in Italy that year
Gross income of over 1.1 million euros in 2024

w: Despite the name, these are the ruins of a Roman villa, not caves: built between the late 1st century BC and early 1st century AD at the tip of the Sirmione peninsula on Lake Garda. Studied by academics since the 15th century, it is now regarded as the finest evidence of the Roman period in northern Italy.
s: A Roman villa mistaken for a grotto, by the lake
_facts: Roman villa ruins, built late 1st century BC to early 1st century AD
Located at the tip of the Sirmione peninsula, Lake Garda
Studied by academics since the 15th century
Considered northern Italy's finest Roman-era site; has its own museum
